title: experiment-contingency-heatmap-and-ops-scripts-wip
body:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a pragmatic contingency heatmap and a set of short, copy-pasteable ops scripts for cross-functional rollout, canary, and A/B experiments. The goal is to give oncall, product, and platform engineers a single reference that maps observed signals to concrete actions, comms templates, and escalation steps.

Scope and intended audience:
- Audience: product managers, release engineers, SREs, oncall, data science/analytics, solutions engineers.
- Scope: staged releases, canary/partial traffic experiments, A/B experiments that change inference model variants or routing, short-lived feature flags, fallback and graceful-degradation scenarios.
- Not covered: long-running model retrain lifecycle, billing disputes, or legal escalations.

High-level philosophy:
1) Make decisions from signals, not feelings: map 6–8 high-value signals to deterministic actions.
2) Prefer reversible, low-friction mitigations first (traffic tilt, reduce batch size, increase fallback).
3) Keep comms scripts short; prefer templates the oncall can send immediately.
4) Prioritize user-visible severity and safety signals over coarse infrastructure warnings.

Contingency heatmap (textual):
Legend: critical = red, elevated = orange, degraded = yellow, nominal = green. Column = cause cluster, row = signal. Actions are ordered: immediate mitigation -> short-term rollback -> full rollback.

Signals and mapped hotspots:
- Latency tail (p99) spike > 2x baseline for 5m: critical (red) if p95 also > 1.5x and error-rate rising. Actions: reduce canary slice by 75%, route canary to slower-but-stable fallback model, trigger pager.
- Error rate (4xx/5xx increase) > 3x baseline in canary slice for 3m: critical. Actions: immediately pause canary traffic, flip to control routing, collect traces and recent PRs, notify product + SRE.
- Semantic regression (eval set failure rate increase > 8% absolute): elevated (orange). Actions: pause rollout, revert model weight to stable version, run quick causal diff on prompts, schedule postmortem.
- Cost spike (per-token cost up >50% vs expected for the slice): degraded (yellow). Actions: throttle canary QPS by 50%, enable token caps, alert finance and product if persists >1h.
- User complaints / legal flags: critical (red) at any volume. Actions: immediate feature kill, full rollback, executive notification.
- Telemetry divergence (embedding drift or distribution shift beyond 3 std dev): elevated. Actions: reduce exposure, run batch eval, tag dataset, schedule model owner review.

Concrete ops scripts and comms (copy/paste):
1) Oncall immediate step (latency spike)
- Slack DM to #oncall-sre: "paging: p99 latency on canary (svc-llm-rerank) 2.8s (baseline 0.9s) over last 5m. Reducing canary from 10%->2% and rerouting to fallback model. Will follow up with traces. @product-steward @eng-serving-runtime FYI"
- Command: "redwoodctl rollout scale --route canary --pct 2 --reason 'p99 latency spike'"
- Telemetry query to attach: "SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95), percentile(latency_ms, 99) FROM requests WHERE slice='canary' AND window=5m"

2) Pause canary (errors increasing)
- Slack to experiment channel: "Pausing canary: errors 5xx up 4x in 3m. Action: set canary traffic=0, fallback to control. Assigned oncall: @{owner}."
- Command: "redwoodctl rollout set-traffic --slice canary --pct 0 --fallback control-v1 --note 'autosafety pause due to 5xx increase'"
- Immediate checklist: collect top 20 traces, export recent model logs (last 30m), open incident ticket JIRA-XXXX and tag analytics.

3) Comms template for product update (short):
Subject: Canary paused for [feature/model name]
Body: "Quick update: At [time] we paused the canary for [experiment id] due to an elevated error rate. Canary traffic is routed back to control. Engineering is collecting traces and we'll share a follow-up within 2 hours. If you have active user sessions impacted, notify support with ticket #JIRA-XXXX."

4) Rapid rollback script (when semantic regressions detected)
- Command: "redwoodctl model promote --from stable-v3 --to live --force --note 'rollback due to eval regression'"
- Post-rollback actions: run smoke tests on critical flows (smokesuite/run.sh), notify stakeholders, schedule 1hr deep-dive.

Telemetry checks and example queries (ops-friendly):
- Error rate by slice: "metric: requests.errors.rate(slice) over 5m window"
- Latency distribution: "p50/p90/p95/p99 per slice over last 15m"
- Prompt distribution shift: compare embedding centroids on rolling 1h vs 7d baseline
- Cost per token: aggregated by model variant every 1m
- Semantic eval: run a subset of golden prompts (100) and compute pass/fail ratio

Simulation scenarios + expected playbook:
- Scenario A: p99 latency doubles after a config flip. Playbook: reduce slice -> toggle kernel optimization off -> if >10m persist, revert config.
- Scenario B: sudden 5xx spike only for one region. Playbook: drain region traffic for that slice, failover to secondary region, attach region-tagged traces.
- Scenario C: A/B shows statistically significant drop in NPS for variant B after 48h. Playbook: stop variant B exposure, run stratified analysis, prepare rollback PR if causality strong.

Decision tree (short form):
1) Is user-visible surface impacted (yes/no)?
- If yes -> prioritize user recovery (rollback/kill); page product lead and SRE.
- If no -> evaluate cost/perf/quality metrics and choose conservative mitigation (reduce exposure, reroute).
2) Is metric trend transient (<10m) or sustained (>30m)?
- Transient: wait + monitor; Sustained: act immediately.
3) Can we route to a compatible fallback model with minimal integration risk?
- If yes: route and observe. If no: reduce exposure and prepare rollback.

Escalation path and responsibilities (one-liners):
- Oncall SRE: first responder for infra/latency/errors, executes rollout control commands.
- Experiment owner (product): decides on user-facing rollback and stakeholder comms.
- Model owner (applied-ml): investigates semantic regressions and coordinates model-promote/revert.
- Solutions/PS: monitors key enterprise customers and runs manual checks if needed.

Quick post-incident checklist (to attach to JIRA):
- Time of detection, first action taken, who executed action, brief signal copy, link to traces, list of impacted experiments, mitigation outcome, next steps, tentative RCA owner.

Open questions and unresolved items (working):
- Should the heatmap live inside Console as codified runbook steps (yes) or remain a Drive doc? Tradeoffs: discoverability vs edit friction.
- Exact numeric thresholds (p99 x2 vs x1.5) need calibration by service; propose starting conservative and iterating.
- Who has automatic permission to flip canary traffic for Dedicated customers? Policy needs defining.

Appendix: useful links and quick commands
- redwoodctl rollout docs: https://internal.redwood/docs/redwoodctl/rollout
- Tracing playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/tracing
- Experiment naming convention: exp/<product>-<short>-YYYYMMDD

Next steps (near-term):
- Run 3 tabletop drills with product + SRE + applied-ml in March (simulate latency spike, semantic regression, region error spike). Owner: Ravi.
- Push a short RFC to codify 3 default threshold profiles (low/medium/high sensitivity). Owner: Avery.
- Prototype embedding-drift alert in Console for one active experiment. Owner: Sasha.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep templates <3 sentences. Always include experiment id and immediate action.
- Prefer traffic tilt over full rollback where possible to gather more signal while minimizing impact.

Document history: initial draft 2025-02-12, iterated with SRE Feb 20, added comms templates Mar 1.
